stance_basis: raises scope interpretation concern and claims significant emissions penalty, implying standard is too stringent without adjustments
summary: International Harvester raised two distinct concerns in comments to the NPRM: first, that the proposed standard's scope inadvertently included vehicles above 6,000 pounds GVWR due to ambiguous language in proposed Part 523; and second, that the 1979 EPA emissions standards would impose a 10–15 percent fuel economy penalty on manufacturers. NHTSA responded to both concerns, rejecting the scope misinterpretation and ultimately concluding that manufacturers failed to demonstrate any fuel economy penalty from the tighter emissions standard, though it did acknowledge an 8 percent testing procedure effect.
complaint_summary: International Harvester estimated that the fuel economy penalty resulting from the 1979 EPA emissions standard would be 10–15 percent, challenging NHTSA's assumption of no fuel economy penalty from the revised emissions standards and testing procedures.
summary_quote: International Harvester believes the penalty due to the emission standard will be 10 - 15 percent.

mentions.quote: International Harvester commented that, although the preamble to the NPRM indicated that only vehicles 6,000 pounds or less, GVWR, were intended to be subject to the standard, the proposed standard as drafted includes in its scope vehicles less than 10,000 pounds GVWR.
International Harvester believes the penalty due to the emission standard will be 10 - 15 percent.
